description: Four bandpass filters locked to whole-number harmonics of one fundamental, so each band lands exactly on a partial of the sound going in

params.text: Sets the fundamental by hand, four octaves either side of 261.63Hz, and does nothing while the menu has the fundamental followed from the audio
Sets the bandwidth of every band as a fraction of the fundamental, 0.02 to 2 times it, so every harmonic is isolated as cleanly as every other
Picks which whole-number harmonic that band tunes to, 1 to 32, where 1 is the fundamental itself
Sets that band's level, silence to full
Switches that band in or out, with a short fade so it does not click

inputs.text: Sets the fundamental as a volt per octave, added to the tune knob; it does nothing while the menu has the fundamental followed from the audio
Changes the bandwidth, added to the width knob at a fifth per volt
Slides every band between harmonics at once, one harmonic per volt, which sweeps the whole bank up and down the series
The signal the bands filter, and the signal the fundamental is detected from while the menu has that switched on
Slides that band between harmonics, one harmonic per volt, added to its harmonic knob
Changes that band's level, added to its level knob at a tenth per volt, so 10V opens it fully
Any voltage at or above 1V switches that band on, and while a cable is here that jack replaces the band's own button

outputs.text: The four bands summed, each at its own level, clamped to -12 to 12V
The four bands on four polyphonic channels, one band per channel, for treating each harmonic separately

notes: the bandwidth is a fraction of the fundamental rather than of each band's own frequency, so the sharpness rises with the harmonic number and every partial is isolated equally well
menu: Follow input pitch (auto-lock harmonics) — finds the fundamental from the audio going in and locks the harmonic grid to it, which takes the TUNE knob and the V/OCT jack out of the picture
Filter slope — a label over the two choices below it
4-pole (steep, default) — gives each band a steeper skirt, which isolates a partial more cleanly
2-pole (gentler) — gives each band a gentler skirt, which lets more of the neighbours through
